subject.title: fix(sessions): capping pass clears all unprotected entries when preserved count exceeds max — cron failures

question: When preserved session entries exceed `maxEntries`, should enforcement continue removing all eligible entries while active lifecycle entries are explicitly protected, or should the cap pass stop entirely?
rationale: The linked cron failure needs repair, but the PR also selects a permanent retention policy already identified as requiring maintainer judgment in the broader durable-pointer report.

options.title: Protect active entries, retain cap
options.body: Keep existing bounded-store semantics and pass the in-flight cron identity through the maintenance preservation contract.

options.title: Pause only above the cap
options.body: Skip capping when preserved entries exceed the limit, with explicit retention behavior, operator guidance, and growth coverage.

options.title: Resolve the broader policy first
options.body: Pause this PR and decide durable-pointer retention in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107750 before changing enforcement behavior.

recommendation.title: Protect active entries, retain cap
recommendation.body: Keep existing bounded-store semantics and pass the in-flight cron identity through the maintenance preservation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent session fixes were rewritten and landed through steipete, providing the clearest current ownership signal for this policy boundary.
